column1: # Shared instant-cache key vectors (#705, #771). Read by ALL FOUR
# implementations of the Unix path -> cache-key encoder and its on-disk
# chunking, so they cannot drift apart again:
# Format: one vector per line, tab-separated: input<TAB>expected<TAB>stem.
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. Extra columns after
# `stem` are reserved for later issues and MUST be ignored by readers that do
# not know them. No column may be empty (tab is IFS-whitespace to bash/zsh
# `input` uses the same mini escape scheme as json_escape_vectors.tsv --
# backslash first: \\ -> one literal backslash byte, \n -> LF, \r -> CR,
# \t -> tab. `expected` is literal (the Unix key never contains a backslash,
# tab or newline) and is NOT unescaped.
# Unix scheme: exactly five escapes, `_` first: _->__ /->_s \->_b :->_c
# space->_w. Every other byte, including the Windows-reserved ? * < > " |,
# passes through unchanged. Every reader MUST fail if this file is missing or
# `stem` (#771) is the cache file's path relative to the instant-prompts
# directory, minus its `.{suffix}.{token}.{ext}` tail: the key itself when it
# is at most 200 characters, else the key split into 50-character chunks
# joined by `/` (every chunk but the last is a directory). Each reader
# asserts the relative path `{stem}.git.none.{ext}` its builder produces.
# Rows over 200 characters contain no tab or newline (Fish chunks
# line-wise). Non-ASCII rows count characters, which Bash/Zsh match only
# under a UTF-8 locale (the readers set one).
